signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using a Harris Corporation address block. Harris is named in EFForg/rayhunter#1000 as a cell-site-simulator vendor. A match means only that hardware from this vendor is nearby; Harris ships a great deal of non-surveillance equipment.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 00-17-F3 assigned to Harris Corporation
EFForg/rayhunter#1000 names Harris among IMSI-catcher manufacturers
signatures.notes: Corroborating evidence only. Never raise this above informational on its own.

signatures.description: Second Harris Corporation address block. Same caveats as imsi.harris.oui.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 00-06-EC assigned to Harris Corporation

signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using an Octasic address block. Octasic is named in EFForg/rayhunter#1000; its DSP and SDR parts appear in cellular test and interception equipment as well as in ordinary telecoms gear.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 00-0C-90 assigned to Octasic Inc.
EFForg/rayhunter#1000 names Octastic/Octasic among IMSI-catcher manufacturers

signatures.description: Nine-nibble MA-S allocation attributed to KeyW Corporation. The parent block 70:b3:d5 belongs to the IEEE Registration Authority and is shared by many small assignees, so only the full nine-nibble prefix is meaningful; matching 70:b3:d5 alone would fire on unrelated hardware.
evidence: EFForg/rayhunter#1042 comment by cooperq (EFF) identifying 70:b3:d5:7c:b as KeyW
IEEE MA-L public registry: 70-B3-D5 is the IEEE Registration Authority MA-S parent block, not an end-vendor assignment
signatures.notes: Provenance is the upstream PR discussion; not independently re-verified against the IEEE MA-S registry here. This is the signature that motivates nibble-precision prefix matching.

signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using the Flock Safety address block.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: B4-1E-52 assigned to Flock Safety
signatures.notes: Reachable from BSS scanning only if the camera transmits a beacon or probe response. Community research (flock-you) reports that Flock's management access point was withdrawn around December 2025 and that current units emit wildcard probe requests instead, which BSS scanning cannot see. Treat a non-detection as uninformative.

signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using the Axon Enterprise address block.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 00-25-DF assigned to Axon Enterprise, Inc.
signatures.notes: Deliberately excludes 'Axon Networks Inc.' (00-58-28, 00-C0-D4) and 'Axonne Inc.' (FC-85-96), which are unrelated companies whose names merely resemble Axon Enterprise. OUI-SPY's Axon detection combines a MAC/OUI with a Bluetooth company identifier and a BLE service UUID; the composite is expressible in this schema but needs BLE input, which the RC400L cannot provide.

signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using the Ring LLC address block. Consumer camera hardware: extremely common in residential areas and not evidence of targeted surveillance.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 54-E0-19 assigned to Ring LLC
signatures.notes: High base rate in residential environments. Kept informational so it can corroborate a persistence finding without generating standalone alerts.

signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using a DJI address block. A nearby drone is not by itself evidence of surveillance; this belongs in the drone category of the UI, not the surveillance category.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 48-1C-B9 assigned to SZ DJI TECHNOLOGY CO.,LTD

signatures.description: Second DJI address block. Same caveats as drone.dji.oui.481cb9.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 60-60-1F assigned to SZ DJI TECHNOLOGY CO.,LTD

signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using the Skydio address block. Drone category, not surveillance category.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 38-1D-14 assigned to Skydio Inc.

signatures.description: Wi-Fi interface using a Parrot SA address block. Drone category, not surveillance category.
evidence: IEEE MA-L public registry: 90-3A-E6 assigned to PARROT SA

signatures.description: Locally-administered transmitter prefix reported by the DeFlockJoplin research and carried in flock-you. Not an IEEE assignment, so it cannot be checked against the public registry.
evidence: colonelpanichacks/flock-you (MIT), target_ouis table, attributed to DeFlockJoplin
signatures.notes: Disabled by default: field-reported, not independently verified here. This prefix has the locally-administered bit set, which is why it needs allow_locally_administered; flock-you explicitly warns that a blanket randomisation filter drops it. Scoped to the transmitter so that an access point merely answering the camera does not match.

signatures.description: Composite: a reported Flock transmitter prefix sending a wildcard probe request. This is the tier-3/4 behaviour flock-you describes, where the camera enumerates networks by asking every access point to identify itself.
evidence: colonelpanichacks/flock-you (MIT), README describing wildcard-probe behaviour at ~0.125s intervals
signatures.notes: Disabled by default, and additionally unreachable on the Orbic RC400L: probe requests require monitor mode, which the QCA9377's qcacld-2.0 build does not expose. Retained so the rule is ready when a capture source that can see probe requests is available (companion radio, or a platform whose driver supports monitor mode).

signatures.description: Strongest reported Flock signature: vendor prefix, wildcard probe behaviour, and a matching information-element fingerprint. Element fingerprinting of probe requests is a documented identification technique (Pintor and Atzori, 2022).
evidence: Pintor, L. & Atzori, L. (2022). Analysis of Wi-Fi Probe Requests Towards Information Element Fingerprinting. GLOBECOM 2022, 3857-3862. doi:10.1109/GLOBECOM48099.2022.10001618
signatures.notes: Disabled by default. The element ID sequence here is a PLACEHOLDER and must be replaced with a sequence captured from a real device before this rule is ever enabled. Enabling it as written would produce meaningless results. Also unreachable on the RC400L for the same reason as research.flock.nitekry.wildcard-probe.
